label: conj:unmodified
title: Conjecture
head: environment
name: Dimension conjecture

title: Remark
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
    		\item Gouv\^{e}a's dimension conjecture \cite[Section~4]{Gouvea2001}
    		allows arbitrary finite sets $S$, i.e., it does not require $S$ to
    		contain the primes of $K$ above $p$.
    		In this broader setting, Bleher and Chinburg
    		\cite[Theorem~1.1]{BleherChinburg2007} constructed counterexamples
    		over infinitely many real quadratic fields, with $p=2$ and
    		$S=\varnothing$. The author also constructed counterexamples over
    		every number field, with ramification sets disjoint from the
    		primes above $p$; see \cite[Theorem~1.7]{Luo2026}. These examples do not provide counterexamples to Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified}, since their sets $S$ do not contain all primes above $p$.
    		
    		\item If the absolute irreducibility of $\bar{\rho}$ is replaced by the weaker condition
    		$\operatorname{End}_{k[G_{K,S}]}(\bar\rho)=k$, then a universal deformation ring still exists; see \cite[Proposition~1.3.1(b)]{Boeckle2013}. However, the dimension conjecture can fail for such reducible residual representations, even when $S$ contains all primes above $p$ and all archimedean primes; see \cite[Section~4]{Boeckle1998}.
    		
    		\item On the positive side, Xinyao Zhang recently proved
    		Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} for $K=\mathbb Q$, $n=2$, and $p\ge3$
    		when $\bar\rho$ is odd and its restriction to the local Galois group $G_{\mathbb Q_p}$ at $p$ is reducible;
    		see \cite[Theorem~A.2.2 and Corollary~A.3.3]{Zhang2026}.
    		These results give that $R_{\bar{\rho}}$ is flat over $W(k)$ with $\dim R_{\bar\rho}=4$, and hence $\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/pR_{\bar\rho})=3=\delta(\bar\rho)$.
    	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
    With notation as above, we have
    \[ \dim R_{\bar\rho}\ge D(K,n)+1, \]
    and every irreducible component $Z$ of
    $\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})$ satisfies
    \[
    \dim Z\ge D(K,n)=\delta(\bar\rho)+C(\bar\rho).
    \]
    In particular, if $C(\bar\rho)>0$, then every such component has
    dimension strictly greater than $\delta(\bar\rho)$, and
    Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} fails.
head: environment

label: rem:odd-prime
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:odd-prime}
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item When $n=1$, every $s_v$ is zero and
		$\lfloor(n-2s_v)^2/2\rfloor=0$. Thus $C(\bar\rho)=0$ in rank one.
		If $K$ is totally imaginary, then $S_{\mathbb R}=\varnothing$, and hence $C(\bar\rho)=0$ for every $n$. In either case, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} gives the usual lower bound.
		
		\item At a real prime $v$, the special fiber of the framed deformation ring has dimension $\lfloor n^2/2\rfloor$, while the residual conjugacy orbit has
		dimension $2s_v(n-s_v)$; see Lemma \ref{lem:real-special}. The sum of these differences over the real
		primes is $C(\bar\rho)$. The usual framed local tangent obstruction count gives the orbit
		dimension. The relative global presentation and the surjectivity of
		restriction in degree two to the real primes allow us to use the
		actual local special fiber dimensions instead, yielding the global
		special fiber lower bound $\delta(\bar\rho)+C(\bar\rho)$. See the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}.
		
		\item In odd residue characteristic, $2$ is invertible, and hence the $1$-eigenspaces and
		$-1$-eigenspaces of an involution are direct summands whose ranks
		remain fixed under deformation. Choosing bases in these summands
		puts every deformation into the same diagonal form. Hence all framed
		local deformations arise by conjugation, and the local special fiber
		has the same dimension as the residual conjugacy orbit. Their
		dimension difference, and therefore the analogous correction, is zero.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:lift
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:lift}
	We keep the notation as above. Suppose that $\rho:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_F)$ is a continuous representation with reduction $\bar\rho\otimes_k k_F$, where $F$ is a finite extension of the field $W(k)[1/2]$, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_F$
	and residue field $k_F$. For $v\in S_{\mathbb R}$, let $a_v$ and $b_v$ denote the multiplicities of the eigenvalues $1$ and $-1$ of $\rho(c_v)$, respectively. Put
	\[ 	D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)=1+n^2r_2(K)
	+2\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}a_vb_v. \]
	Then we have the following.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item One has 
		\[
		\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})\ge D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)=\delta(\bar\rho)+2\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}
		(a_v-s_v)(b_v-s_v).
		\]
		In particular, Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} fails if
		$s_v<\min(a_v,b_v)$ for some $v\in S_{\mathbb R}$.
		\item One has
		\[ 	\dim R_{\bar\rho}-\operatorname{depth}R_{\bar\rho}\geq D(K,n)-D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)-\dim_F H^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad}(\rho\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F)).  \]
	 where $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\bar{\rho}})$ denotes the depth of the ring $R_{\bar{\rho}}$. Moreover, if
	 \[ D(K,n)-D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)>\dim_F H^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad}(\rho\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F)), \]
	 then $R_{\bar\rho}$ is not equidimensional, not Cohen--Macaulay, and not a complete
		intersection.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: rem:lift-correction
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:lift-correction}
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The correction in Theorem~\ref{thm:lift}\textup{(1)} comes from
		comparing the dimension lower bounds obtained from the residual
		and characteristic-zero Euler characteristic formulas.
		For $V=\rho\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F$, their common term
		$1+(r_1(K)+r_2(K))n^2$ cancels, giving
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)-\delta(\bar\rho)
			&=\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}
			\bigl(\dim_k(\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho)^{c_v=1}
			-\dim_F(\operatorname{ad} V)^{c_v=1}\bigr)\\
			&=2\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}(a_v-s_v)(b_v-s_v).
		\end{aligned}
		\]
		Thus the correction measures the increase in the real adjoint
		invariant dimensions under reduction. Obstruction theory and the
		residual Euler characteristic formula give
		$\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})\ge\delta(\bar\rho)$.
		The characteristic-zero formula at the point defined by $\rho$
		similarly gives $\dim R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]\ge D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)$.
		The inequality $\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})\ge\dim R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$
		transfers the latter bound to the special fiber.
		
		\item For odd prime $p$, the projectors $(I_n\pm\rho(c_v))/2$ preserve the
		eigenspace ranks and hence the adjoint invariant dimensions under
		reduction, and hence the analogous correction vanishes.
		
		\item For every characteristic-zero lift $\rho$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:lift},
		the equality $a_v+b_v=n$ implies that $D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)\le D(K,n)$.
		Thus the special fiber bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:lift}\textup{(1)}
		is numerically no stronger than that in Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
		and its counterexample criterion implies $C(\bar\rho)>0$.
		The main additional contribution of Theorem~\ref{thm:lift} lies in
		part~\textup{(2)}. 
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: cor:example
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cor:example}
		Let $K$ be a number field with $r_1(K)>0$ and $\operatorname{disc}(K)$ be the discriminant of $K$. Let $E$ be the elliptic curve over $K$ defined by 
		\[ y^2=x^3-36|\operatorname{disc}(K)|^2 m^2x+1,
		\]
		where $m$ is a fixed positive integer.
		Let $S$ be the set consisting of all primes of $K$ above $2$, all archimedean primes of $K$, and all primes of bad reduction of $E$. Denote by
		$\rho:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_2)$ and
		$\bar{\rho}:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_2)$ the
		representations on $T_2(E)$ and $E[2]$, respectively. Then the following statements hold.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item $\bar{\rho}$ is absolutely irreducible with
			$C(\bar{\rho})=2r_1(K)>0$, and $\rho$ satisfies
			$s_v<\min(a_v,b_v)$ for every $v\in S_{\mathbb R}$. Moreover, every irreducible component $Z$ of
			$\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})$ satisfies
			\[
			\dim Z-\delta(\bar\rho)\ge2r_1(K)>0.
			\]
			In particular, Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} fails for $\bar\rho$.
			
			\item If $K$ is totally real, then the ring $R_{\bar{\rho}}$
			is not equidimensional, not Cohen--Macaulay, and not a
			complete intersection.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: cor:tower
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cor:tower}
        Let $K,E,S,\rho$, and $\bar\rho$ be as in
        Theorem~\ref{cor:example}, and choose a prime
        $\ell\nmid6[K:\mathbb Q]$. For $r\ge0$, let $F_r$ be the unique
        degree-$\ell^r$ subfield of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{\ell^{r+1}})$, where
        $\zeta_{\ell^{r+1}}$ is a primitive $\ell^{r+1}$th root of unity. Put
        $K_r=KF_r$ and $E_r=E\times_K K_r$. Let $S_r$ consist of
        the primes of $K_r$ above $S$, and let
        \[
        \rho_r:G_{K_r,S_{r}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_2),\qquad
        \bar\rho_r:G_{K_r,S_{r}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_2)
        \]
        be the two-dimensional representations on $T_2(E_r)$ and
        $E_r[2]$, respectively, obtained by restricting $\rho$ and
        $\bar\rho$. Then the following statements hold.
        \begin{enumerate}
        	\item $\bar\rho_r$ is absolutely
        	irreducible with $ C(\bar\rho_r)>0$, and $\rho_r$ satisfies $s_v<\min(a_v,b_v)$ at every real
        	prime of $K_r$. Moreover, every irreducible component $Z_r$ of
        	$\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho_r}/2R_{\bar\rho_r})$ satisfies
        	\[
        	\dim Z_r-\delta(\bar\rho_r)\ge2\ell^r r_1(K)>0.
        	\]
        	That is, Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} fails throughout the
        	tower, with discrepancy tending to infinity uniformly over
        	all irreducible components of the special fibers.
        	
        	\item If $K$ is totally real, then each $R_{\bar\rho_r}$ is not equidimensional,
        	not Cohen--Macaulay, and not a complete intersection.
        \end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: cor:all-ranks
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cor:all-ranks}
    For every number field $K$ with $r_1(K)>0$ and every $n\ge2$,
    there are a finite set $S_{K,n}$ of primes of $K$ containing
    all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes, and a continuous
    absolutely irreducible representation
    \[
    \bar\rho_{K,n}:G_{K,S_{K,n}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_4)
    \]
    whose unrestricted universal deformation ring $R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}$
    satisfies
    \[
    \dim(R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}/2R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}})>\delta(\bar\rho_{K,n}).
    \]
    Thus Conjecture~\ref{conj:unmodified} fails for $\bar\rho_{K,n}$.
    Moreover, if $K$ is totally real, then $R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}$ is not a
    complete intersection.
head: environment

label: totallyeven
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{totallyeven}
	It is worth pointing out that our examples in
	Theorems~\ref{cor:example}, \ref{cor:tower}, and~\ref{cor:all-ranks}
	above simultaneously satisfy the counterexample criteria of
	Theorems~\ref{thm:main} and~\ref{thm:lift}\textup{(1)}.
	Moreover, all the residual representations in these examples are
	\emph{totally even}, meaning that $\bar\rho(c_v)=I_n$ for every
	real prime $v$ of $K$, where $c_v$ denotes a complex conjugation.
head: environment

label: lem:residual-centralizer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:residual-centralizer}
We have $0\le s_v\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. The Jordan form of
$\bar\rho_v(c_v)$ has $s_v$ blocks of size two and $n-2s_v$ blocks
of size one, and
\[
\dim_k(\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho_v)^{G_v}
=(n-s_v)^2+s_v^2=n^2-2s_v(n-s_v).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The matrix $N_v=\bar\rho_v(c_v)-I_n$ satisfies $N_v^2=0$.
As a $k[T]$-module, with $T$ acting by $N_v$, one has
\[
k^n\simeq\bigl(k[T]/(T^2)\bigr)^{s_v}
\oplus\bigl(k[T]/(T)\bigr)^{n-2s_v}.
\]
The space of homomorphisms from $k[T]/(T^i)$ to $k[T]/(T^j)$ has
dimension $\min(i,j)$. The endomorphism algebra is the centralizer
of $\bar\rho_v(c_v)$, and hence its dimension is
\[
2s_v^2+2s_v(n-2s_v)+(n-2s_v)^2=(n-s_v)^2+s_v^2.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:real-special
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:real-special}
The ring $R_v^{\square}/2R_v^{\square}$ has Krull dimension $d_n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Modulo $2$, the substitution $X=I_n+N$ changes $X^2=I_n$
into $N^2=0$. Over an algebraic closure of $k$, the square-zero
matrices of rank $q$, for $0\le q\le m:=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$,
form one conjugacy class, of Jordan type $(2^q,1^{n-2q})$.
Its stabilizer is the open set of units in its centralizer algebra.
The calculation in Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-centralizer} therefore
gives its dimension as
\[
n^2-((n-q)^2+q^2)=2q(n-q).
\]
Every such class lies in the closure of the rank-$m$ class:
multiply the upper-right entries of $m-q$ size-two blocks by a
parameter and specialize it to zero, then conjugate.
Thus the variety of square-zero matrices is irreducible of
dimension $2m(n-m)=d_n$. Since $k$ is perfect, the reduced
coordinate ring
\[
T=(A_n/2A_n)_{\mathrm{red}}
\]
is geometrically integral of dimension $d_n$.

Since $T$ is a finite-type domain over $k$, its localization at
the maximal ideal induced by $J_v$ has dimension $d_n$
\cite[Tag~02IJ]{Stacks}. Reduction modulo $2$ commutes with
Noetherian local completion. Removing nilpotents and completing
preserve Krull dimension \cite[Tag~07NU]{Stacks}, which proves
the assertion.
head: environment

label: lem:balanced-real-lift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:balanced-real-lift}
The representation $\bar\rho_v$ has a lift
$\rho_v:G_v\to\operatorname{GL}_n(W(k))$ such that the eigenvalues $1,-1$
of $\rho_v(c_v)$ over $F$ have multiplicities
\[
a=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\qquad b=\lceil n/2\rceil,
\]
respectively.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In a Jordan basis, each size-two block lifts to
\[
H=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad H^2=I_2.
\]
The matrix $H^{\oplus s_v}\oplus I_{a-s_v}\oplus(-I_{b-s_v})$
has the required reduction and eigenvalue multiplicities.
Lift the change of basis to $\operatorname{GL}_n(W(k))$ and conjugate back;
the resulting matrix defines $\rho_v(c_v)$.
head: environment

label: prop:real-base
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:real-base}
For every real prime $v$, we have
\[
\dim R_v^{\square}=1+d_n.
\]
For a family $(\bar\rho_v)_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}$, let
\[
B=\mathop{\widehat{\bigotimes}}\limits_{\substack{v\in S_{\mathbb R}\\W(k)}}R_v^{\square},
\]
where completion is taken with respect to the ideal generated by
the maximal ideals of the factors. If $S_{\mathbb R}=\varnothing$, then we
set $B=W(k)$. Then we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:real-base-dimensions}
\dim(B/2B)=r_1(K)d_n,\qquad \dim B=1+r_1(K)d_n.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $\operatorname{Spec}(B/2B)$ is equidimensional.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove the assertion for $R_v^{\square}$.
Let $a=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and $b=\lceil n/2\rceil$.
Over $F$, the conjugacy class of $\operatorname{diag}(I_a,-I_b)$
is closed and geometrically integral, of dimension
\[
n^2-a^2-b^2=2ab=d_n.
\]
Indeed, every involution is semisimple, and its trace determines
the two multiplicities. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A_n$ be the
contraction of the prime ideal defining this conjugacy class in
$A_n[1/2]$. Then $A_n/\mathfrak p$ is a domain containing $W(k)$,
and its fraction field has transcendence degree $d_n$ over $F$.
Evaluation at the lift in Lemma~\ref{lem:balanced-real-lift}
kills $\mathfrak p$, so $\mathfrak p\subset J_v$.
The dimension formula over the universally catenary discrete
valuation ring $W(k)$ gives
\[
\dim(A_n/\mathfrak p)_{J_v/\mathfrak p}=1+d_n
\]
\cite[Tag~02IJ]{Stacks}. The surjection
\[
R_v^{\square}\twoheadrightarrow
\widehat{(A_n/\mathfrak p)_{J_v/\mathfrak p}}
\]
therefore gives $\dim R_v^{\square}\ge1+d_n$.
Conversely, the principal ideal dimension inequality and
Lemma~\ref{lem:real-special} give
\[
\dim R_v^{\square}
\le1+\dim(R_v^{\square}/2R_v^{\square})=1+d_n.
\]

We now prove the assertions for $B$. They are immediate if
$S_{\mathbb R}=\varnothing$. Otherwise, form the ordinary tensor product
\[
A_{S_{\mathbb R}}=\bigotimes_{v\in S_{\mathbb R},W(k)}A_n,
\qquad
J=\ker\left(A_{S_{\mathbb R}}
\xrightarrow{\,\bigotimes_v\varepsilon_v\,}k\right).
\]
Here each factor is evaluated at its own $\bar\rho_v(c_v)$.
The completed tensor product satisfies
\[
B\simeq\widehat{(A_{S_{\mathbb R}})_J}.
\]
Indeed, both rings represent tuples of framed lifts of the
$\bar\rho_v$. In the notation of the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:real-special},
\[
(A_{S_{\mathbb R}}/2A_{S_{\mathbb R}})_{\mathrm{red}}
\simeq\bigotimes_{v\in S_{\mathbb R},k}T.
\]
This is a geometrically integral $k$-algebra of dimension
$r_1(K)d_n$. Localizing at the maximal ideal induced by $J$ and
completing, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:real-special}, gives
$\dim(B/2B)=r_1(K)d_n$.
The same calculation also proves equidimensionality after completion.
Indeed, the localization of
$(A_{S_{\mathbb R}}/2A_{S_{\mathbb R}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ at the
maximal ideal induced by $J$ is a local domain essentially of finite
type over $k$, hence is universally catenary. By Ratliff's theorem,
its completion is equidimensional
\cite[Tags~0AW2 and~0AW6]{Stacks}. The natural surjection from
$B/2B$ to this completion has nilpotent kernel, since completion
is exact on finite modules over a Noetherian local ring.
It therefore induces a homeomorphism on spectra.

For the integral dimension, take the product over $F$ of the
conjugacy classes used in the single-prime argument. It is
geometrically integral of dimension $r_1(K)d_n$.
Let $\mathfrak P\subset A_{S_{\mathbb R}}$ be the contraction
of its defining prime ideal in $A_{S_{\mathbb R}}[1/2]$.
The lifts from Lemma~\ref{lem:balanced-real-lift}, chosen for every
$v$, give an evaluation map $A_{S_{\mathbb R}}\to W(k)$ that
kills $\mathfrak P$ and reduces to the map defining $J$.
Thus $\mathfrak P\subset J$. The same dimension formula gives
\[
\dim(A_{S_{\mathbb R}}/\mathfrak P)_{J/\mathfrak P}
=1+r_1(K)d_n.
\]
Its completion is a quotient of $B$, so
$\dim B\ge1+r_1(K)d_n$. The reverse inequality follows from
$\dim B\le1+\dim(B/2B)$.
head: environment

label: rem:rank-two-real-flatness
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rank-two-real-flatness}
For $n=2$, the dimension statements in
Proposition~\ref{prop:real-base} are well known.
In this case, the rings $R_v^{\square}$ are $2$-torsion-free and
hence flat over $W(k)$. In particular, we have 
\[
\dim(B/2B)=2r_1(K),\qquad \dim B=1+2r_1(K).
\]
The calculation in \cite[Section~5.5]{Boeckle2013} concerns odd
deformations. For $n>2$, Proposition~\ref{prop:real-base} establishes the stated dimensions and the equidimensionality of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/2B)$,
without establishing $W(k)$-flatness of $R_v^{\square}$.
head: environment

label: lem:relative-relations
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:relative-relations}
Let $B\to A$ be a map of complete Noetherian local $W(k)$-algebras
with residue field $k$, and put
\[
t=\dim_k\mathfrak m_A/(\mathfrak m_A^2+\mathfrak m_BA).
\]
Then $A$ is a quotient of $B[[X_1,\ldots,X_t]]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ lifting a basis of the relative
cotangent space. Sending the $X_i$ to these elements defines a
map $B[[X_1,\ldots,X_t]]\to A$, which is surjective by Nakayama's
lemma and completeness.
head: environment

label: prop:relative-global
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Absolute irreducibility implies that the matrices $\bar\rho(g)$ span
$M_n(k)$, by Burnside's theorem after extension to an algebraic closure.
Choose $n^2$ such matrices forming a basis. For every lift over $C$,
their lifts form a $C$-basis of $M_n(C)$ by Nakayama's lemma; hence
its centralizer consists of scalars.
Fix a representative of the universal deformation over $R_{\bar\rho}$.
The choices of frames are then $r_1(K)$ matrices in
$I_n+M_n(\mathfrak m_C)$ modulo simultaneous multiplication by
$1+\mathfrak m_C$. Normalizing the $(1,1)$-entry of one frame to $1$
removes this scalar uniquely and leaves $r_1(K)n^2-1$ free parameters.
This proves \eqref{eq:global-frame-parameters} and gives $B\to A$.

The induced tangent map is
\[
\theta:T_A\longrightarrow T_B
=\bigoplus_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}Z^1(G_v,\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho).
\]
Varying the frames supplies all local coboundaries, so
\[
\operatorname{coker}\theta\simeq
\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{res}^1),
\qquad
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{res}^0)
\longrightarrow\ker\theta
\longrightarrow\ker(\operatorname{res}^1)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since $H^0(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho)=k$ and $S_{\mathbb R}\ne\varnothing$,
$\operatorname{res}^0$ is injective. Hence $\dim_k\ker\theta=t$,
and Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-relations} gives a minimal presentation
\[
\varphi:P=B[[X_1,\ldots,X_t]]\twoheadrightarrow A.
\]

We bound its relations by following the proof of
\cite[Key Lemma~5.2.2, Section~5.6]{Boeckle2013}, using $\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho$
in place of the trace-zero adjoint module.
Put $J=\ker\varphi$, let $\mathfrak m_P$ be the maximal ideal of
$P$, and set $E=J/\mathfrak m_PJ$. Nakayama's lemma gives
$\mu(J)=\dim_k E$. Consider the square-zero extension
\[
0\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow P/\mathfrak m_PJ
\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow0.
\]
For $u\in E^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(E,k)$, pushing out along $u$
gives an extension of complete local $W(k)$-algebras
\[
0\longrightarrow I_u\longrightarrow P_u
\xrightarrow{\,\varphi_u\,}A\longrightarrow0,
\qquad I_u\simeq k,\quad\mathfrak m_{P_u}I_u=0.
\]
Choose a representative $(\rho_A,(\gamma_{v,A})_v)$ of the universal
$S_{\mathbb R}$-framed deformation over $A$ and a continuous
set-theoretic lift $\widetilde\rho_u:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(P_u)$.
Such a lift exists: the surjection $\operatorname{GL}_n(P_u)\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$
has finite kernel and admits a continuous set-theoretic section,
obtained by choosing coset representatives for an open subgroup
on which it is injective.
Its multiplicative defect defines a continuous cocycle
\[
\widetilde\rho_u(g)\widetilde\rho_u(h)
\widetilde\rho_u(gh)^{-1}=I_n+z_u(g,h),
\qquad z_u\in Z^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad}\bar\rho).
\]
The class $[z_u]$ is independent of the lift and vanishes precisely
when $\rho_A$ lifts to a representation over $P_u$.
These classes are contractions of the obstruction class with
coefficients in $E$, so $u\mapsto[z_u]$ is $k$-linear.
The map $B\to P_u$ supplies local framed lifts; conjugating by
lifts of the $\gamma_{v,A}$ gives lifts of $\rho_A|_{G_v}$.
Thus every local restriction of $[z_u]$ vanishes, and we obtain
\[
\alpha:E^\vee\longrightarrow\ker(\operatorname{res}^2),
\qquad u\longmapsto[z_u].
\]

It remains to bound $\ker\alpha$. Put
\[
K_0=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{ct}(P)\to\operatorname{ct}(A)\bigr).
\]
There is a natural surjection
$\beta:E\twoheadrightarrow K_0$, induced by $J\subset P$.
Since the images of the $X_i$ form a basis of the relative
cotangent space, the decomposition
$\operatorname{ct}(P)=\operatorname{ct}(B)\oplus k^t$ identifies
\[
K_0\simeq\ker\bigl(\operatorname{ct}(B)\to\operatorname{ct}(A)\bigr),
\qquad K_0^\vee\simeq\operatorname{coker}\theta.
\]
For $0\ne u\in\ker\alpha$, lift $\rho_A$ and all its frames
to $P_u$. Universality gives a $W(k)$-algebra section
$s:A\to P_u$ of $\varphi_u$.
The decomposition $P_u=s(A)\oplus I_u$, together with
$\mathfrak m_{P_u}I_u=0$, implies
\[
\mathfrak m_{P_u}^2+2P_u=s(\mathfrak m_A^2+2A).
\]
Hence $I_u$ injects into $\operatorname{ct}(P_u)$.
If $e\in\ker\beta$, its image in $\operatorname{ct}(P_u)$ is zero,
while its image in $I_u\simeq k$ is $u(e)$. Thus $u(e)=0$.
Consequently $u$ factors uniquely through $K_0$, giving a linear
injection $\ker\alpha\hookrightarrow K_0^\vee$.
It follows that
\[
\mu(J)=\dim_k E
\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\theta
+\dim_k\ker(\operatorname{res}^2)=o.
\]
Finally, $\dim P=\dim B+t$, and quotienting by at most $o$
elements gives $\dim A\ge\dim B+t-o$.

label: lem:dimension-drop
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dimension-drop}
		Let $(C,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $t\in\mathfrak m$.
		Then $\dim C/tC\ge\dim C-1$.  If $C[1/t]\ne0$, then
		\[
		\dim C[1/t]\le\dim C-1\le\dim C/tC.
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Every chain of prime ideals of $C$ avoiding $t$ can be extended by
		appending $\mathfrak m$, which proves the first inequality in the
		display.  For the other inequality, put $d=\dim C/tC$ and lift a system
		of $d$ parameters of $C/tC$ to $y_1,\ldots,y_d\in C$.
		The ideal $(t,y_1,\ldots,y_d)$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary.
		Krull's height theorem gives $\dim C\le d+1$.

label: lem:component-dimension
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:component-dimension}
Let $C$ be an equidimensional complete Noetherian local ring of
dimension $e$, and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$ be generated by at
most $o$ elements.
Then every irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$ has dimension
at least $e-o$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For any prime $\mathfrak p$ minimal over $I$,
choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C$ contained in
$\mathfrak p$. Then $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q$ is minimal over
$(I+\mathfrak q)/\mathfrak q$, so its height is at most $o$.
Since $C/\mathfrak q$ is a catenary local domain of dimension $e$,
\[
\dim(C/\mathfrak p)
=e-\operatorname{ht}_{C/\mathfrak q}(\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q)
\ge e-o.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $D=D(K,n)$ and $d_n=\lfloor n^2/2\rfloor$.

If $r_1(K)=0$, \cite[Proposition~1.5.1]{Boeckle2013} gives
\[
R_{\bar\rho}\simeq W(k)[[x_1,\ldots,x_{h^1}]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m),
\qquad m\le h^2.
\]
Since $\dim W(k)=1$, Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-euler} implies
\[
\dim R_{\bar\rho}\ge1+h^1-h^2=2+n^2r_2(K)=D+1.
\]
Reducing the presentation modulo $2$ and applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:component-dimension} to the regular local ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_{h^1}]]$
shows that every irreducible component of
$\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})$ has dimension at least
$h^1-m\ge h^1-h^2=D$.

Suppose now that $r_1(K)>0$. Let $B$ be the completed tensor
product over $W(k)$ of the real framed deformation rings, and
let $A$ represent global deformations with a frame at each real
prime. By Proposition~\ref{prop:relative-global},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:global-relative-presentation}
A\simeq R_{\bar\rho}[[u_1,\ldots,u_{r_1(K)n^2-1}]],\qquad
A\simeq B[[x_1,\ldots,x_t]]/J,\qquad \mu(J)\le o.
\end{equation}
At each real prime, the periodic resolution of $C_2$ has
alternating differentials $c_v-1$ and $1+c_v$. These coincide
in characteristic two, and hence $h_v^1=h_v^2$.
Together with Lemma~\ref{lem:real-surjectivity}, the tangent and
relation counts in Proposition~\ref{prop:relative-global} give
\[
\begin{split}
t-o
&=h^1-h^2+\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}(h_v^0-h_v^1+h_v^2)-1\\
&=h^1-h^2+\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}h_v^0-1\\
&=n^2(r_1(K)+r_2(K)),
\end{split}
\]
where the last equality follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-euler}
and $h^0=1$. Proposition~\ref{prop:real-base} gives
$\dim B=1+r_1(K)d_n$. Thus
\eqref{eq:global-relative-presentation} yields
\[
\begin{split}
\dim R_{\bar\rho}
&=\dim A-(r_1(K)n^2-1)\\
&\ge\dim B+t-o-(r_1(K)n^2-1)\\
&=2+n^2r_2(K)+r_1(K)d_n=D+1.
\end{split}
\]

To prove the componentwise assertion when $r_1(K)>0$, put
$N=r_1(K)n^2-1$ and reduce the relative presentation modulo $2$:
\[
(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})[[u_1,\ldots,u_N]]
\simeq (B/2B)[[x_1,\ldots,x_t]]/\bar J,
\qquad \mu(\bar J)\le o.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:real-base}, the power series ring on the
right is equidimensional of dimension $r_1(K)d_n+t$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:component-dimension} shows that every component of
$\operatorname{Spec}(A/2A)$ has dimension at least $r_1(K)d_n+t-o$.
The minimal primes of a formal power series ring over a Noetherian
ring are the extensions of the minimal primes of its coefficient
ring, and adjoining $N$ variables increases each component's
dimension by $N$. Thus, for every irreducible component $Z$ of
$\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})$, we have
\[
\dim Z\ge r_1(K)d_n+t-o-N
=1+n^2r_2(K)+r_1(K)d_n=D.
\]
Finally, the identity
\[
d_n-2s(n-s)=\left\lfloor\frac{(n-2s)^2}{2}\right\rfloor
\qquad(s\in\mathbb Z)
\]
and Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-euler} give
$D=\delta(\bar\rho)+C(\bar\rho)$.
If $C(\bar\rho)>0$, then every component of the special fiber has
dimension strictly greater than $\delta(\bar\rho)$, proving the
final assertion.

label: lem:rational-euler
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rational-euler}
		For any continuous finite-dimensional $F$-representation $\rho$ of
		$G_{K,S}$, we have
		\[
		h^0-h^1+h^2
		=\sum_{v\in S_{\mathbb R}}\dim_F\rho^{c_v=1}
		-(r_1(K)+r_2(K))\dim_F\rho,
		\]
		where $h^i:=\dim_F H^i(G_{K,S},\rho)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: It follows from \cite[Lemma~9.7]{Kisin2003}.
head: environment

label: lem:involution
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The matrices $\rho(c_v)-I_n$ and $\rho(c_v)+I_n$ have ranks $b_v$
		and $a_v$ over $F$, respectively. Their reductions over $k_F$
		are equal and have rank $s_v$, since rank is preserved by
		$k\subseteq k_F$. Specialization gives both inequalities.
		Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-centralizer} and diagonalization over $F$ give
		\[
		(n-s_v)^2+s_v^2-a_v^2-b_v^2=2(a_v-s_v)(b_v-s_v),
		\]
		which is \eqref{eq:invariant-defect}. Combining this identity with
		Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-euler} gives the asserted formula for $D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)$.
		Finally, $n=a_v+b_v$ implies
		\[
		\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{2}\right\rfloor-2a_vb_v
		=\left\lfloor\frac{(a_v-b_v)^2}{2}\right\rfloor,
		\]
		and summation proves \eqref{eq:balanced-gap}.

label: lem:closed-point-components
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:closed-point-components}
Let $x$ be a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec} R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$, with
corresponding prime $\mathfrak P\subset R_{\bar\rho}$, and put
$E_x=\kappa(x)$. Then $E_x/W(k)[1/2]$ is finite, specialization
induces a continuous lift
$\rho_x:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{E_x})$ of $\bar\rho$ after
extending residue fields, and $\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P)=1$.
Put
\[
V_x=\rho_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E_x}}E_x,\qquad
e_x=\dim_{E_x}H^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad} V_x).
\]
Let $\mathfrak m_x=\mathfrak P R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$ be the maximal ideal
corresponding to $x$. Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho_x)\le\dim \widehat{(R_{\bar\rho}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}
\le D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho_x)+e_x.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The assertions about $E_x$, $\rho_x$, and $R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P$
follow from \cite[Lemma~7.1.9 and its proof, pp.~78--79]{deJong1995}.
The representation $V_x$ is absolutely irreducible, since $\rho_x$
has absolutely irreducible reduction. By \cite[Proposition~9.5]{Kisin2003},
$\widehat{(R_{\bar\rho}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}$ is its universal
deformation ring over $E_x$. Write
$h^i=\dim_{E_x}H^i(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad} V_x)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:rational-euler}
gives $h^1-h^2=D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho_x)$.
The presentation in the proof of \cite[Corollary~9.8]{Kisin2003}
has $h^1$ variables and at most $h^2=e_x$ relations, so
\[
h^1-h^2\le\dim \widehat{(R_{\bar\rho}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}\le h^1.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inverse image $\mathcal O_0$ of
$k$ under $\mathcal O_F\to k_F$ is a finite complete local
$W(k)$-algebra with residue field $k$, and $\rho$ takes values
in $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_0)$. Universality gives
$R_{\bar\rho}\to\mathcal O_0\subseteq\mathcal O_F$.
Let $\mathfrak P$ be its kernel. Its image is finite over
$W(k)$ and contains $W(k)$, so
$\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P)=1$. Thus $\mathfrak P$
determines a closed point $x$ of $\operatorname{Spec} R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$,
with residue field $E_x\subseteq F$.

Put $\mathfrak m_x=\mathfrak P R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$ and
\[
A=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec} R_{\bar\rho}[1/2],x}
=(R_{\bar\rho}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}
\cong(R_{\bar\rho})_{\mathfrak P}.
\]
The isomorphism uses $2\notin\mathfrak P$. Set
\[
h^2_\rho=\dim_F H^2
(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad}(\rho\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F)).
\]
The rational representation at $x$ becomes
$\rho\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F$ after extending scalars to $F$.
Real signatures and cohomology dimensions are unchanged
under this finite coefficient extension. Since
\[
\dim A=\dim \widehat{(R_{\bar\rho}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}
\]
by invariance of dimension under completion,
Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-point-components} gives
\[
D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)
\le\dim A\le D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)+h^2_\rho.
\]

For \textup{(1)}, Lemma~\ref{lem:dimension-drop} yields
\[
\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})
\ge\dim R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]\ge\dim A
\ge D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:involution} gives the stated identity and shows
that its correction is positive exactly when
$s_v<\min(a_v,b_v)$ for some $v\in S_{\mathbb R}$.

For \textup{(2)}, choose a minimal prime
$\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak P$ of $R_{\bar\rho}$.
Since $2\notin\mathfrak P$, we have $2\notin\mathfrak q$.
The complete local domain $R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q$
is catenary \cite[Tags~032C and~0ECF]{Stacks}, so
\[
\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)
=\dim(A/\mathfrak qA)+\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P)
\le\dim A+1.
\]
Every minimal prime is associated \cite[Tag~05BV]{Stacks}.
Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lift-component-upper-bound}
\operatorname{depth}R_{\bar\rho}
\le\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)
\le D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho)+h^2_\rho+1.
\end{equation}
Together with Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, this proves the depth bound.
Under the strict inequality in \textup{(2)}, this component
has dimension smaller than $\dim R_{\bar\rho}$, and
$\operatorname{depth}R_{\bar\rho}<\dim R_{\bar\rho}$.
Thus $R_{\bar\rho}$ is neither equidimensional nor
Cohen--Macaulay, and hence is not a complete intersection.

label: prop:even-artin-cohomology
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:even-artin-cohomology}
Let $K$ be a totally real number field and $S$ a finite set of primes
of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes.
Let $F/\mathbb Q_2$ be a finite extension and let
$\rho:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ be a continuous representation with
finite image. Assume that $\rho$ is totally even, that is,
$\rho(c_v)=I_n$ for every $v\in S_{\mathbb R}$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:even-artin-h2-bound}
h_K^2(\rho):=\dim_F H^2(G_{K,S},\rho)
\le\frac{[K:\mathbb Q]\cdot n}{2}.
\end{equation}
The dimension $h_K^2(\rho)$ is independent of $S$ and
unchanged by finite extension of $F$.
If $\rho=\eta|_{G_K}$ for a continuous totally even finite-image
representation $\eta:G_\mathbb Q\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$, then we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:total-real-base-change-defect}
h_K^2(\rho)\le h_\mathbb Q^2(\eta)+\frac{([K:\mathbb Q]-1)n}{2}.
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $V=F^n$ with its given Galois action, let $N/K$ be the
	extension cut out by $\rho$, and put $\Delta=\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)$.
	Let $S_N$ be the set of primes above $S$, and let $\mathcal D_N$
	be the logarithmic kernel in
	\eqref{eq:leopoldt-logarithmic-kernel}, with $N$ in place of $K$.
	Write $(-)^\vee$ for the linear dual. Poitou--Tate duality
	\cite[Chapter~I, Theorem~4.10]{Milne2006},
	after passing to rational coefficients, and Kummer theory give
	a $\Delta$-equivariant isomorphism
	\[
	H^2(G_{N,S_N},\mathbb Q_2)^\vee\simeq\mathcal D_N.
	\]
	Indeed, the local $H^2$ groups with coefficients in $\mathbb Q_2$
	vanish, while the localization kernel on $S_N$-units is
	$\mathcal D_N$: local valuations force its elements to be
	ordinary units, and the remaining conditions are precisely
	the vanishing of their $2$-adic logarithms.
	Hochschild--Serre therefore yields
	\[
	H^2(G_{K,S},V)^\vee
	\simeq
	\operatorname{Hom}_{F[\Delta]}
	\bigl(V,\mathcal D_N\otimes_{\mathbb Q_2}F\bigr).
	\]
	After extending scalars to $\overline{\mathbb Q}_2$, the dimension
	of the right-hand side is the Leopoldt defect
	$\delta_K^L(V\otimes_F\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)$ of
	\cite[(3.10)]{Maksoud2023}.
	Since $K$ is totally real and $V$ is totally even,
	\[
	d^+(V)=
	\sum_{v\mid\infty}\dim_F V^{c_v=1}
	=[K:\mathbb Q]n.
	\]
	Thus \cite[Corollary~4.2(1)]{Maksoud2023} gives
	\[
	h_K^2(\rho)\le\frac{d^+(V)}2
	=\frac{[K:\mathbb Q]n}{2}.
	\]
	The displayed description by $\operatorname{Hom}$ also proves
	independence of $S$ and invariance under finite extension of $F$.

For \eqref{eq:total-real-base-change-defect}, we write $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$ and choose an auxiliary
finite set of rational primes containing $2$, $\infty$, and the
primes where $K/\mathbb Q$ or $\eta$ ramifies. Write
$\operatorname{Ind}_{G_K}^{G_\mathbb Q}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\oplus P_0$.
The representation $P_0$ is totally even of dimension $d-1$.
The projection formula and Shapiro's lemma give
\[
h_K^2(\rho)=h_\mathbb Q^2(\eta)+h_\mathbb Q^2(\eta\otimes_F P_0).
\]
The bound just proved, applied over $\mathbb Q$ to $\eta\otimes_F P_0$,
gives the assertion for $d>1$; the case $d=1$ is immediate.
Independence of $S$ permits the auxiliary enlargement of the
ramification sets.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $N=|\operatorname{disc}(K)|$, $u=3Nm$, and
$f(X)=X^3-4u^2X+1$. Neither possible rational root $\pm1$
is a root, and
\[
(16u^3-1)^2<D:=\operatorname{disc}(f)=256u^6-27<(16u^3)^2.
\]
Thus its splitting field $L/\mathbb Q$ is totally real with Galois
group $S_3$. We claim that $L\cap K^{\mathrm{gal}}=\mathbb Q$,
where $K^{\mathrm{gal}}$ is the normal closure of $K/\mathbb Q$.
Indeed,
\[
D=27Q,\qquad Q=6912(Nm)^6-1.
\]
The positive odd integer $Q$ is congruent to $2$ modulo $3$
and is coprime to $3N$. Hence some odd prime $q\nmid3N$
occurs in $Q$ to an odd power. It ramifies in the unique
quadratic subfield $\mathbb Q(\sqrt D)$ of $L$, whereas
$K^{\mathrm{gal}}$ is unramified at $q$. Thus this quadratic
field is not contained in $K^{\mathrm{gal}}$, and the normal
subgroups of $S_3$ prove the claim.

Consequently $K(E[2])=KL$ has Galois group
$S_3=\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_2)$ over $K$. Its natural representation is
absolutely irreducible: the two elementary transvections
have different unique invariant lines over $\overline{\mathbb F}_2$.
Good reduction outside $S$ gives the stated representations
of $G_{K,S}$
\cite[Chapter~VII, Proposition~5.1(a) and Theorem~7.1]{Silverman2009}.
Since $L$ is totally real, $\bar\rho(c_v)=I_2$ at every
real prime. Thus $s_v=0$ and $C(\bar\rho)=2r_1(K)>0$.
The Weil pairing identifies $\det\rho$ with the $2$-adic
cyclotomic character
\cite[Chapter~III, Proposition~8.3]{Silverman2009};
hence $\rho(c_v)$ has eigenvalues $1,-1$, each once.
Therefore $s_v=0<\min(a_v,b_v)=1$, and both asserted
criteria apply.
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} gives
$\dim Z-\delta(\bar\rho)\ge C(\bar\rho)=2r_1(K)$ for every
irreducible component $Z$ of the special fiber.

To prove \textup{(2)}, we construct another lift $\tau$ of $\bar\rho$, distinct from the Tate-module lift $\rho$.
The permutation action of $\operatorname{Gal}(KL/K)\simeq S_3$ on
\[
\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb Z_2^3:x_1+x_2+x_3=0\}
\]
gives a totally even finite-image lift $\tau$ of $\bar\rho$.

Now suppose that $K$ is totally real. Put $d=[K:\mathbb Q]$,
$L_K=KL$, $T=L_K^{A_3}$, and $V=\tau\otimes_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathbb Q_2$.
The decomposition $\operatorname{ad} V\simeq\mathbf1\oplus\varepsilon\oplus V$,
where $\varepsilon$ is the sign character, gives
\[
(\operatorname{ad} V)^{\oplus2}\simeq
\operatorname{Ind}_{G_{L_K}}^{G_K}\mathbf1
\oplus\operatorname{Ind}_{G_T}^{G_K}\mathbf1.
\]
Shapiro's lemma and the definition of $\lambda$ imply
\[
2\dim_{\mathbb Q_2}H^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad} V)=\lambda(L_K)+\lambda(T).
\]
The fields $L_K$ and $T$ are totally real of degrees $6d$ and
$2d$ over $\mathbb Q$. By \eqref{eq:waldschmidt-bound},
$\lambda(L_K)\le3d-1$ and $\lambda(T)\le d-1$. Hence
\[
\dim_{\mathbb Q_2}H^2(G_{K,S},\operatorname{ad} V)\le2d-1
<2d=D(K,2)-D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\tau),
\]
and Theorem~\ref{thm:lift}\textup{(2)} proves the remaining assertions.

title: Proof
body_md:
The subgroup of order $\ell-1$ in
$(\mathbb Z/\ell^{r+1}\mathbb Z)^\times$ contains $-1$, so $F_r/\mathbb Q$
is totally real and cyclic of degree $\ell^r$.
Since $\ell\nmid[K:\mathbb Q]$, one has $K\cap F_r=\mathbb Q$ and
$[K_r:K]=\ell^r$. Every real prime of $K$ splits completely
in $K_r$, whence $r_1(K_r)=\ell^r r_1(K)$.
Put $L=K(E[2])$. Since $[L:K]=6$ and
$\ell\nmid6$, one has $L\cap K_r=K$. Consequently
$\operatorname{Gal}(LK_r/K_r)\simeq S_3$, so $\bar\rho_r$ remains
absolutely irreducible. Good reduction is preserved by
base change, giving the stated representations of
$G_{K_r,S_r}$.

At every real prime of $K_r$, the residual action is trivial
and the Tate representation has signature $(1,1)$.
Thus $s_v=0<\min(a_v,b_v)=1$ and
\[
C(\bar\rho_r)=2r_1(K_r)=2\ell^r r_1(K).
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} therefore gives the claimed discrepancy
for every irreducible component of the special fiber.
Theorem~\ref{thm:lift}\textup{(1)} independently gives the
same lower bound for its total dimension.

The totally even augmentation-lattice lift restricts to $K_r$.
If $K$ is totally real, so is $K_r$, and the preceding $S_3$
calculation with Waldschmidt's bound applies over $K_r$.
This proves the remaining assertions.

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\mathcal O=W(\mathbb F_4)=\mathbb Z_2[\zeta_3]$ and $a=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$.
We first construct two induced lifts, with signatures $(a,n-a)$
and $(n,0)$, whose common reduction remains absolutely irreducible
over $K$.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Step 1: the inducing character.}
Choose primes $\ell\equiv1\pmod{2n}$ and
$q\equiv1\pmod{3\ell}$, both unramified in the normal closure $K^{\mathrm{gal}}$ of $K/\mathbb Q$;
Dirichlet's theorem permits these choices
\cite[Chapter~VII, Theorem~5.14]{Neukirch1999}.
Let $L$ be the degree-$n$ subfield of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_\ell)$.
Then $L/\mathbb Q$ is cyclic, totally real, and totally ramified at $\ell$,
so $L\cap K^{\mathrm{gal}}=\mathbb Q$.
Moreover $q\mathcal O_L=\mathfrak q_1\cdots\mathfrak q_n$ splits completely.

We need a cubic character of $G_L$ ramified at $\mathfrak q_1$
and unramified at the other primes above $q$. Use Shanks's polynomial
\cite[p.~1138, equations~(3)--(4)]{Shanks1974}
\[
f_t(X)=X^3-tX^2-(t+3)X-1,
\qquad \operatorname{disc}(f_t)=(t^2+3t+9)^2.
\]
Choose an integer $r$ whose reduction is a nontrivial cube root of
unity modulo $q$.
Since $f_{3r}(X)\equiv(X-r)^3\pmod q$ and the coefficient
of $t$ in $f_t(r)$ is $-(r^2+r)\equiv1\pmod q$, there is an integer
$t_0\equiv3r\pmod q$ with $f_{t_0}(r)\equiv q\pmod{q^2}$.
By the Chinese remainder theorem, choose $t\in\mathcal O_L$ with
\[
t\equiv t_0\pmod{\mathfrak q_1^2},\qquad
t\equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak q_i}\quad(i>1).
\]
Then $f_t(X+r)$ is Eisenstein at $\mathfrak q_1$, whereas
its discriminant is a unit at every $\mathfrak q_i$ with $i>1$.
Thus $f_t$ is irreducible with square discriminant, so a root
generates a cyclic cubic extension $M/L$.
A faithful character
$\psi:G_L\to\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)\simeq\mu_3\subset\mathcal O^\times$
has the required ramification, as does its reduction $\bar\psi$.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Step 2: the two lifts and absolute irreducibility.}
Choose $\alpha\in L^\times$ positive at exactly $a$ real embeddings
by weak approximation, and let $\eta$ be the quadratic character
of $L(\sqrt\alpha)/L$.
Using one inducing basis, put
\[
\rho_{K,n}=\left(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_L}^{G_\mathbb Q}(\eta\psi)\right)|_{G_K},
\qquad
\tau=\left(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_L}^{G_\mathbb Q}\psi\right)|_{G_K}.
\]
Both have finite image, consisting of monomial matrices with nonzero
entries in $\mu_6$, and have the same reduction $\bar\rho_{K,n}$.
Since $L$ is totally real and $\psi$ has odd order, their signatures
at every real prime of $K$ are $(a,n-a)$ and $(n,0)$, respectively;
in particular $\bar\rho_{K,n}(c_v)=I_n$.

It remains to check absolute irreducibility. Since
$L\cap K^{\mathrm{gal}}=\mathbb Q$, Mackey's formula gives
\[
\bar\rho_{K,n}\simeq
\operatorname{Ind}_{G_{KL}}^{G_K}(\bar\psi|_{G_{KL}}).
\]
The completions of $KL$ above $q$ are unramified over $\mathbb Q_q$.
Hence the totally ramified cubic extension at $\mathfrak q_1$
remains totally ramified of degree three after base change.
The $n$ conjugates of $\bar\psi|_{G_{KL}}$ therefore remain
ramified above mutually distinct primes $\mathfrak q_i$ and
unramified above the others, so they are pairwise distinct.
Their joint image has odd order. Over $\overline{\mathbb F}_2$, every
invariant subspace for this image is consequently a sum of its
distinct character lines, and $G_K$ permutes these lines transitively.
Thus $\bar\rho_{K,n}$ is absolutely irreducible, also for even $n$.

Let $S_{K,n}$ be the finite set consisting of the primes above $2$,
all archimedean primes,
and all primes ramified in the splitting fields of these two
finite-image representations. Both lifts factor through
$G_{K,S_{K,n}}$, and
\[
C(\bar\rho_{K,n})=r_1(K)\lfloor n^2/2\rfloor>0,
\qquad D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\rho_{K,n})=D(K,n).
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} proves the first assertion.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Step 3: dimension comparison over a totally real field.}
Suppose that $K$ is totally real, and put
$d=[K:\mathbb Q]$, $b=d\lfloor n^2/2\rfloor$, and
$R=R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}$.
Set $F=\mathbb Q_2(\zeta_3)$ and
$V=(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_L}^{G_\mathbb Q}\psi)\otimes_{\mathcal O}F$.
Write $\operatorname{ad}^0V=D^0\oplus W$, where $D^0$ consists of the
traceless diagonal matrices and $W$ of the matrices with zero
diagonal. Both summands are stable under conjugation by the
monomial representation $V$.
Since $L/\mathbb Q$ is cyclic and totally real, after a finite extension
of $F$ the representation $D^0$ splits into one-dimensional
totally even characters. Proposition~\ref{prop:even-artin-cohomology}
gives $h_\mathbb Q^2(\chi)\le1/2$, hence $h_\mathbb Q^2(\chi)=0$, for each
such character. The same proposition gives
$h_\mathbb Q^2(W)\le n(n-1)/2$.
Thus \eqref{eq:total-real-base-change-defect} yields
\[
e_0:=h_K^2(\operatorname{ad}^0V|_{G_K})
\le\frac{n(n-1)+(d-1)(n^2-1)}2
=\frac{d(n^2-1)-(n-1)}2<b.
\]
Since $D_{\mathrm{lift}}(\tau)=1$ and
$h_K^2(\operatorname{ad} V|_{G_K})=\lambda(K)+e_0$,
\eqref{eq:lift-component-upper-bound} gives a minimal prime
$\mathfrak q$ of $R$ not containing $2$ such that
$\dim(R/\mathfrak q)\le2+\lambda(K)+e_0$.

For the lower bound, let $x$ be the characteristic-zero closed point
defined by $\rho_{K,n}$, with $E_x$, $V_x$, and $\mathfrak m_x$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-point-components}.
Since $n$ is invertible in $E_x$, taking the unique $n$th root of
the determinant ratio congruent to one splits the deformation
functor into fixed-determinant deformations and character
deformations. By logarithms and \eqref{eq:leopoldt-h1}, the latter
factor is formally smooth of dimension $1+\lambda(K)$, so
\[
\widehat{(R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}\simeq R_{V_x}^{\det}[[t_1,\ldots,t_{1+\lambda(K)}]],
\]
where $R_{V_x}^{\det}$ is the universal deformation ring of $V_x$
over $E_x$ with determinant fixed to $\det V_x$.
The fixed-determinant presentation, as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-point-components}, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:rational-euler} give
\[
\dim R_{V_x}^{\det}\ge
\dim_{E_x}H^1(G_{K,S_{K,n}},\operatorname{ad}^0V_x)
-\dim_{E_x}H^2(G_{K,S_{K,n}},\operatorname{ad}^0V_x)
=b,
\]
using absolute irreducibility and the real signatures $(a,n-a)$.
Catenarity, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:lift}, gives
\[
\dim R\ge\dim \widehat{(R_{\bar\rho_{K,n}}[1/2])_{\mathfrak m_x}}+1\ge2+\lambda(K)+b.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{depth}R\le\dim(R/\mathfrak q)
\le2+\lambda(K)+e_0<2+\lambda(K)+b\le\dim R.
\]
Thus $R$ is not equidimensional, not Cohen--Macaulay, and not a
complete intersection.

label: conj:two-dimensional-Q
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:two-dimensional-Q}
Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $2$, let $S$ be a finite
set of places of $\mathbb Q$ containing $2$ and $\infty$, and let
\[
\bar\rho:G_{\mathbb Q,S}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(k)
\]
be a continuous absolutely irreducible representation. Let
$R_{\bar\rho}$ be the unframed universal deformation
ring of $\bar{\rho}$ over $W(k)$. Then every irreducible component $Z$ of
$\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})$ satisfies
\[
\dim Z=3.
\]
Moreover, if $\bar\rho(c)\ne I_2$, where $c$ denotes a complex
conjugation, then $R_{\bar\rho}$ is flat over $W(k)$ and is a
complete intersection.

title: Remark

label: prop:conjectural-dimensions
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:conjectural-dimensions}
Let $\bar\rho$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Conjecture~\ref{conj:two-dimensional-Q}, and assume that
the conjecture holds for $\bar\rho$.
Then
\[
\dim R_{\bar\rho}=4,\qquad \dim R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]=3.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:dimension-drop}, we have
$4\le\dim R_{\bar\rho}\le1+\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})=4$.
Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ with $\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)=4$.
Since $\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/2R_{\bar\rho})=3$, we have $2\notin\mathfrak q$ and hence $(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)[1/2]\ne0$.
Choose a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec} R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]$ on this component,
corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak P\supseteq\mathfrak q$ of $R_{\bar\rho}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-point-components}, we have
$\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P)=1$.
By catenarity of the complete local domain $R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q$
\cite[Tags~032C and~0ECF]{Stacks},
\[
\dim\bigl((R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak P/\mathfrak q}\bigr)
=\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak q)-\dim(R_{\bar\rho}/\mathfrak P)=3.
\]
Thus $\dim R_{\bar\rho}[1/2]\ge3$, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:dimension-drop} gives the reverse inequality.
